Chronic bone and joint infection is a devastating disease.

the activation of NK cells in chronic bone and joint infections due to staphilococci.
the study of natural killer cells (NK cells) and their activation in patients with chronic bone and joint infections.
the role of NK cells in the pathogenesis of chronic BJI due either to staphyloccocal SCVs or other bacteria.

the NK cells are activated in patients with chronic bone and joint infection due to staphlococci expressing SCVs.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NK cells in patients suffering from chronic bone and joint infections due to staphlococci expressing the small colony variant phenotype are activated in terms of expression of CD69 and loss of CD16.
chronic BJI due Staphylococcus aureus or S. epidermidis are associated with an activation of peripheral blood natural killer cells, independently of the small colony variant phenotype.

The main takeaway from our work is that
NK cells are activated in chronic bone and joint infection, independently of the type of staphylococcus involved and the presence of the SCV.
the activation of natural killer cells is associated to the persistence of chronic infection, and is not specific for a given pathogen.
the phenotype of NK cells in patients infected with staphylococcus expressing or not the small colony variant phenotype is very similar, and that NK cells in patients are activated.
